name: Scrim
desc: The frame stops being a screen and becomes cloth — the live canvas is re-projected onto a hanging theatrical gauze, domain-warped column by column so a wave travels through it, the bunched folds turning away from the key and pooling shadow while the facing flanks catch sheen, all pinned at the edges under the projector's own falloff.

energy.doc: fold depth — how far the cloth throws the image and how hard the folds shade

scale.doc: fold wavelength — a few broad swags or fine pleating

density.doc: fold count across the cloth (and the slice resolution that carries them)

sheen.doc: specular return off the flanks facing the key

hue.doc: cloth + fold-shadow hue (210 = cool stage gauze)

speed.doc: how fast the wave travels through the cloth

x.doc: key-light side — 0 or 1 rakes the folds hard, 0.5 is frontal and flattens them (the fold shadows stay either way)

y.doc: projector centre — where the beam's falloff is brightest

alpha.doc: master opacity of the whole pass

style.doc: what the frame is projected onto
